summary.goal: Connect mull to the plannr monorepo's actual data sources. The generic core reads files; this integration layer reads from our SQLite databases and daemon storage. Three distinct adapters (planner.db, forge.db, relay daemon), each a separate concern with different schemas and data shapes. Plus server plugin mount for HTTP access and event-driven triggers for real-time memory extraction during live sessions. These adapters live alongside the generic core in packages/mull/ but are clearly separated — they import from the project's storage packages.
in_scope: Planner DB adapter: reads DecisionEvent from planner.db trajectory_events table
Forge DB adapter: reads TrajectoryEvent (40+ types) + Retrospective + UserTrajectoryEvent + DerivedPreference from forge.db
Relay daemon adapter: reads from .agent-relay/ SQLite or JSONL archives
Express plugin mount at /api/mull for server integration
REST endpoints: POST /run (trigger), GET /status (stats), GET /topics, GET /topics/:slug
Event-driven triggers: deterministic on decision/chapter events, LLM batched on threshold/timer/session-end
out_of_scope: UI for viewing memory (agents use grep/ripgrep/tilth)
Modifying any existing planner/forge/relay data (mull is read-only)
Relay SDK dependency in generic adapters (that stays in integration)

acceptance_criteria.description: Planner adapter reads DecisionEvents from planner.db and produces SessionData with populated decisions[]
Forge adapter reads TrajectoryEvents from forge.db and maps 40+ event types to appropriate SessionEvent types
Forge adapter maps Retrospective (summary, approach, decisions[], challenges[], learnings[], suggestions[], confidence) to SessionData.retrospective
Forge adapter maps UserTrajectoryEvent (user decision patterns) as high-signal Decision inputs
Forge adapter maps DerivedPreference (confidence-scored learned preferences) as Context nugget candidates
Relay daemon adapter reads from .agent-relay/ daemon storage — both SQLite and JSONL fallback
Multi-adapter merge: planner decisions + forge trajectory + relay messages for same plan/run merged by timestamp
POST /api/mull/run accepts { sessionId?, planId?, runId?, force? } and triggers mull pipeline
GET /api/mull/status returns { topicCount, lastUpdated, recentSessions[], memoryDir }
Event-driven: deterministic layer runs on decision_recorded, retrospective_recorded, chapter_start events
Event-driven: LLM layer batches and runs when 3+ new entities accumulated or timer (20 min) or session ends
All integration adapters are read-only — never modify source databases

observations: Three distinct data sources with completely different schemas — each needs its own adapter, not one monolithic adapter
Planner DecisionEvent: question_text, options_presented, selected_option, reasoning → maps cleanly to Decision type

Forge has 40+ event types but only ~10 are high-signal for mull: decision_recorded, checkpoint_created, retrospective_recorded, agent_spawned, task_completed, task_failed, gate_reached, budget_warning
Forge Retrospective is richer than spec's generic interface: has approach, decisions[] with linked_event_ids, suggestions[] — these are all valuable nugget sources
UserTrajectoryEvent captures user decision patterns with scope (global/project/run) — already-distilled preferences
DerivedPreference has confidence scores and evidence counts — valuable metadata for nugget confidence
Session ID mapping: planner uses plan_id, forge uses run_id, relay uses its own session concept — need mapping layer
Server plugin follows existing pattern: export createRouter(), mount at /api/mull
Event triggers align with existing SSE patterns in the server
concerns: Schema coupling: integration adapters depend on planner/forge storage schemas — version changes need coordination
Real-time triggers must be non-blocking — extraction in <100ms, but LLM batching needs background processing
Session identity: how does a 'plan_id' in planner map to a 'run_id' in forge? They're different lifecycle stages of same work.

architect.planner_trajectory_table: trajectory_events: event_id TEXT PK, type TEXT, question_id TEXT, asking_agent TEXT, question_text TEXT, context_provided TEXT, options_presented_json TEXT, selected_option TEXT, free_text_response TEXT, reasoning TEXT, plan_id TEXT FK, step_id TEXT, timestamp TEXT
architect.forge_trajectory_table: trajectory_events: event_id TEXT PK, run_id TEXT FK, task_id TEXT FK, event_type TEXT, payload TEXT (JSON), timestamp TEXT
architect.forge_retrospective_shape: { summary: string, approach: string, decisions: [{question, chosen, reasoning, linked_event_ids?}], challenges: string[], learnings: string[], suggestions: string[], confidence: number }
architect.forge_user_trajectory_table: user_trajectory_events: event_id TEXT PK, user_id TEXT, scope TEXT, question_text TEXT, selected_option TEXT, reasoning TEXT, run_id TEXT, task_id TEXT, project_id TEXT, category TEXT, timestamp TEXT
architect.forge_user_preferences_table: user_preferences: preference_id TEXT PK, user_id TEXT, scope TEXT, category TEXT, value TEXT, confidence REAL, evidence_count INTEGER, last_expressed TEXT, is_override INTEGER, created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT
architect.relay_storage: .agent-relay/messages/ directory with YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl files; daemon also has SQLite in .agent-relay/
